title: Amino Acid Chart: Test Yourself on All 20 Codes and pKa
description: All 20 amino acids with one and three letter codes, pKa, pI, mass and hydropathy, plus a seven question self test you can take on the page itself.
intro: Seven questions pulled straight from the chart below, so you can see what you actually remember instead of just looking it up again.

questions.q: Glutamine's one-letter code is which of these?
questions.why: G and E are already spoken for by glycine and glutamate, so glutamine and asparagine fall back to Q and N.
questions.source: AA: Gln.c1 (Q); distractors Gly.c1, Glu.c1, Asn.c1

questions.q: Which of these has a side chain pKa listed in the chart?
questions.why: A pkr value only appears for side chains that actually gain or lose a proton, which the phenol does and the amides and alcohols do not.
questions.source: AA: Tyr.pkr = 10.07; Gln.pkr, Thr.pkr, Asn.pkr are all null

questions.q: Of these four, which has the highest pI?
questions.why: pI follows the side chain charge, and the guanidinium group holds its proton to a far higher pH than an imidazole or an amine.
questions.source: AA: compare pI across Arg, Lys, His, Asp

questions.q: Which set does the chart list as the Aromatic class?
questions.why: The class column goes by the side chain's defining feature, so histidine is filed under its basic ring rather than with the aromatics.
questions.source: AA: cls for Phe, Trp, Tyr = Aromatic; His = Basic, Ser = Polar, Met = Nonpolar

questions.q: Which one does the chart mark as essential?
questions.why: The chart splits the 20 into nine essential, six conditional and five you make freely, so conditional is not a softer word for essential.
questions.source: AA: Leu.ess = Yes; Gly.ess and Pro.ess = Conditional, Ala.ess = No

questions.q: Three of these sit in the Nonpolar class. Which one does not?
questions.why: Both cysteine and methionine carry sulfur, but only the thiol ionizes, and that is what moves it out of the nonpolar group.
questions.source: AA: Cys.cls = Polar (pkr 8.18); Met.cls, Pro.cls, Val.cls = Nonpolar

questions.q: Which of these scores as the most hydrophobic?
questions.why: On the Kyte-Doolittle scale the branched aliphatic chains outscore an aromatic ring, so a big greasy-looking side chain is not automatically the top one.
questions.source: AA: compare hyd across Ile, Val, Leu, Phe
